Let \(p\equiv 1\pmod 4\) be any prime such that \(p\nmid y\). Since \(-1\) is a quadratic residue modulo \(p\), there exists \(a\not\equiv0\pmod p\) satisfying
\[
(ay)^2\equiv-1\pmod p.
\]
Write \(p-1=2^e s\), where \(e\ge2\) and \(s\) is odd. By the Chinese remainder theorem, choose \(b\) such that
\[
b\equiv3\pmod{2^e},\qquad b\equiv2\pmod{q^v}
\]
for every maximal odd prime power \(q^v\mid p-1\). Then
\[
\gcd(b,p-1)=1,\qquad \gcd(b-1,p-1)=2.
\]
Indeed, \(b\) is coprime to every prime divisor of \(p-1\); moreover, \(b-1\equiv2\pmod{2^e}\) and \(b-1\equiv1\pmod q\) for every odd \(q\mid p-1\).

Because \(\gcd(p,p-1)=1\), choose by the Chinese remainder theorem an integer \(r\) satisfying
\[
r\equiv a\pmod p,
\qquad r\equiv b\pmod{p-1}.
\]
The preceding properties give \(\gcd(r,p(p-1))=1\). Hence Dirichlet's theorem supplies a prime \(\ell\) with
\[
\ell\equiv r\pmod{p(p-1)}.
\]
Since \(\ell\equiv a\pmod p\), we have
\[
p\mid(\ell y)^2+1.
\]
Applying the hypothesis with \(n=\ell\), and using \(\varphi(\ell)=\ell-1\), yields
\[
p\mid x^{\ell-1}-1.
\]
Thus \(p\nmid x\). Let \(d=\operatorname{ord}_p(x)\). Then
\[
d\\mid\ell-1\quad\text{and}\quad d\mid p-1.
\]
Also, because \(\ell\equiv b\pmod{p-1}\),
\[
\gcd(\ell-1,p-1)=\gcd(b-1,p-1)=2.
\]
Consequently \(d\mid2\), so \(x^2\equiv1\pmod p\). Therefore every prime \(p\equiv1\pmod4\) not dividing \(y\) divides \(x^2-1\).

There are infinitely many primes congruent to \(1\pmod4\), while only finitely many primes divide \(y\). Hence infinitely many primes divide the fixed integer \(x^2-1\), which is possible only if \(x^2-1=0\). Since \(x\) is positive, \(x=1\).
input.theorem:
Let \( x \) and \( y \) be positive integers. If for each positive integer \( n \) we have that

\[
(n y)^{2}+1 \mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1
\]

prove that \( x=1 \).
